Test result: S11 MAE 0.4184 dB, resonant-freq MAE 0.0283 GHz, functioning classification 80.02%; permutation sensitivity 0.29 dB.

Kaggle notebook that builds all 114,797 PyG graphs (25x25: 99,833; 35: 4,988; 45: 6,984; 55: 2,992) with the same build_pyg_graph, makes a joint stratified 80/10/10 split (stratified by grid_size x is_functioning; 91,837/11,480/11,480; random_state=42), and computes per-frequency-point S11 mean/std from the joint training split of all four grids (79,866/3,990/5,587/2,394 for 25/35/45/55): these are the canonical s11_mean.npy/s11_std.npy every later chunk loads (mean range [-5.619,-0.044], std range [0.014,7.161]).

CPU-only Kaggle notebook defining GATv2Block and AntennaGNN (4 blocks x 2 GATv2 layers, hidden 128, 8 heads, edge_dim 16, metal-only mean pool + virtual-node embedding -> MLP -> 201 outputs; 587,001 params), verifying output shapes across 25/45/55 grids and gradient flow, and writing src/model.py.

Colab notebook training AntennaGNN on the 25x25 subset (79,866 train / 9,984 val) with Adam lr1e-3 wd1e-4, batch 128, ReduceLROnPlateau(0.5,5), grad-clip 1.0, dropout 0.10, early stop patience 20, MSE on z-scored S11, resuming from a Drive checkpoint at epoch 112. Best val MSE (normalised) 0.688534 at epoch 111; early stopped at epoch 131.

Evaluates GNN (best_model.pt) vs CNN (cnn_best.pt) on the 25x25 test set (9,983): S11 MAE 0.3742 dB (GNN) vs 0.3913 (CNN), RMSE 1.1478 vs 1.1356, resonant-freq MAE 0.0210 vs 0.0207 GHz, functioning accuracy 80.26% vs 80.24%. Also band-stratified MAE, cost table (GNN 587,001 vs CNN 6,163,473 params), data-efficiency curves (GNN 0.434 vs CNN ~0.54 dB at 20k), and permutation test (CNN 0.42 dB vs GNN 3.4e-7 dB).

Subclasses AntennaGNN to return GATv2 attention weights from the last layer of the last block, builds per-pixel attention heatmaps (mean over 8 heads, metal-metal edges only, aggregated per target node, min-max normalised) and plots pattern/attention/S11 panels for 9 functioning and 4 non-functioning 25x25 test antennas. Qualitatively, functioning antennas show attention along continuous metal paths from the feed; non-functioning ones show scattered or isolated-island attention.

Tests whether BFS path length from the feed predicts resonant frequency (poor: in-band R of L vs 1/f only ~0.05-0.09; R_all -0.20 to -0.57 over 5,485 functioning test antennas) and runs a counterfactual ablation flipping the 10 highest-attention vs 10 distance-matched low-attention metal pixels on 50 antennas. Paired Wilcoxon on median ||dS11||: p=0.037, path>offpath in 30/50; pooled Mann-Whitney p=0.004; discrete peak shift not significant (p=0.63).

Subclasses AntennaGNN to extract the 256-d post-readout_proj embedding for 9,983 25x25 test graphs (UMAP fit on 10k train embeddings, n_neighbors=30, min_dist=0.1) and relates it to resonant frequency, path length and gain. Headline: PCA-1D manifold axis vs resonant freq Spearman rho=0.78; zero-shot 35/45/55 grids embed near frequency-matched 25x25 neighbours (median kNN delta_f 0.098 GHz vs 0.237 random, 2.41x; 5.06x/2.32x/1.08x per grid); gain correlates best with electrical size sqrt(A)/lambda (rho=0.891); raw .mat has no angular pattern data.

Builds PyG graphs (frozen build_pyg_graph copied from Chunk 5) for the 35x35, 45x45, 55x55 fine-tune grids (14,964 samples; 63.4/65.3/48.4% functioning), writes manifest and pool/val/test splits (11,971/1,496/1,497, reusing Chunk 5 indices.json) and defines FinetuneDataset that z-scores y at load with the 25x25 s11_mean/s11_std. Smoke test: zero-shot weighted val S11 MAE 0.6717 dB (was ~3.9 in v1.0 with broken normalisation); 5 epochs of full fine-tune (lr 1e-4) gives 0.3580 dB, grad norm clipped ~99.7% of steps at max_norm 1.0.

Compares four fine-tune strategies (A full lr1e-4, B freeze 2 blocks, C freeze 3 blocks, D full lr5e-4) plus a clip-threshold control A-hi on a 2,000-sample stratified pool subset with z-scored targets. Strategy A wins (weighted val S11 MAE 0.3524 dB vs zero-shot 0.6717; B 0.3553, C 0.3588, D 0.3675, A-hi 0.3539); on test, A beats zero-shot per grid (35: 0.5689->0.3711, 45: 0.6915->0.3187, 55: 0.7234->0.3606 dB), though resonance detection rate stays ~47-49%.
